articleTitle: From biochip to integrated biochemical analysis system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biosensors: A Viable Monitoring Technology?
abstract: The rapid development of IC-technology has strongly stimulated the fabrication of (bio)chemical sensors based on solid-state devices. Principally, such (bio)chemical sensors consist of a (bio)chemically sensitive membrane combined with a signal transducing solid-state chip. It has appeared that a crucial point in the development of such sensors is the well-controlled and reproducible deposition of the sensitive membranes on the underlying structure. Therefore, the authors have developed different techniques to deposit and pattern polymeric membranes on whole wafers. In this way not only a reproducible membrane deposition is obtained, but also the advantages of bathwise production are maintained. ISFET based devices and amperometric sensors are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New development in quartz crystal biosensors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biosensors: A Viable Monitoring Technology?
abstract: The authors discuss modification of quartz crystal resonant oscillator surfaces by appropriate organic compounds leading to development of biosensors. The essential feature of quartz crystal biosensors is that they respond to the structural changes consequent on the analyte-sensor molecule binding process. They can be unique sensitive detectors of bio-interactions provided the responses are properly interpreted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

abstract: The author discusses the basic physics underlying the evanescent field biosensor and the requirements for surface plasmon generation. The practical realisation of such immunosensors is also examined. The combination of surface plasmon resonance and fluorescence immunoassay to give a surface plasmon resonance enhanced fluorescence immunoassay is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Biomembrane properties and their reproduction in vitro. (Biosensor application)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biosensors: A Viable Monitoring Technology?
abstract: The author discusses fundamental biomembrane properties and the application of such membranes in biosensors. Lipid bilayers and membrane proteins involved in transfer mechanisms are examined. Classes of transport mechanism are illustrated. The reconstitution of transport system types is discussed for non-biological environments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
